plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Rolling rows of silvery-green shrubs erupt into waves of violet-blue flower spikes. The warm, herbal scent drifts across the hills and hums with bees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-June to late August, with peak bloom in July
plants.funFact: The name lavender likely comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'. The Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: Huge pink and white blooms rise on tall stalks above round, water-repellent leaves. They open at dawn across ponds and paddies, and each flower can reach about a foot across.
plants.bloomingSeason: July to August (early summer through midsummer)
plants.location: Ponds and lakes across temperate Asia, including Japan and China
plants.funFact: Lotus leaves have a microscopic surface texture that sheds water and dirt. Engineers call this the 'lotus effect' and copy it in self-cleaning materials.

plants.name: Banksia ericifolia
plants.description: Dense heath-like shrubs carry glowing orange-gold flower spikes that look like bottlebrushes. In the Australian winter they feed nectar-loving birds and small mammals.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early or mid-winter (March to July)
plants.location: Coastal eastern Australia, around New South Wales
plants.funFact: Banksias often depend on fire. Their woody cones can hold seeds for years and release them after bushfires.
